Subject: Re: Oxbridge RFP - IP & Liability questionnaire (attached)

Rafael/Karthik — initial legal notes below (high level):

1) Output ownership / model improvements:
- Redwood cannot assign IP in the underlying model weights. For customer-provided inputs and the resulting outputs, we propose a licence-to-use model: Oxbridge gets a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use outputs generated from their data for internal clinical purposes.
- We will not use customer data to re-train general-purpose public models without an explicit opt-in. We can offer a dedicated model variant (private instance) that guarantees no training on aggregated customer content.

2) Liability cap:
- Standard Redwood cap: aggregate liability limited to the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim.
- For healthcare-critical integrations, we can increase to 24 months' fees for a defined subset of claims (data breach causing regulated PHI exposure or proven patient harm), conditional on: higher SLA (99.95% uptime for the dedicated pool) and mandatory incident table-top exercises quarterly.

3) Indemnity:
- Redwood offers mutual indemnity for third-party IP infringement for trained models and delivered outputs, with a carve-out for customer-supplied prompts or data that include third-party proprietary content.

4) Order form / data retention:
- We will list retention windows (30/90/365 days) by dataset class — default 90 days for KV caches, 365 days for audit logs (can be shortened on request).

I will prepare a redline of the Order Form and proposed language for the IP section. James (external counsel) will likely push back on the scope of the output licence.

- Laura
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redlines_OrderForm_Oxbridge_v1.docx

From: James Li <james.li@gibsonlaw.com>

Date: 2026-10-04T09:27:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Oxbridge RFP - IP & Liability questionnaire (attached)

Laura — thanks for the early read. A few points from counsel:

- Oxbridge's priority is clarity on "output ownership" when outputs are directly used in patient-facing workflows. They are not asking Redwood to transfer model weights but want a guarantee that outputs and derivative works created from their patient data are fully owned by Oxbridge. The proposed perpetual licence is a good start, but they will request assignment for outputs and derivatives used in production clinical workflows.

- On liability, Oxbridge's procurement group will not accept a cap that is effectively fees-only for patient-harm claims. They will request carve-outs for regulatory fines and a higher uncapped or higher-capped regime for proven patient harm.

- On data use: they want explicit language prohibiting any form of model improvement that uses their PHI, including metadata, without express written consent.

They understand some of these asks are non-starters; the ask is for Redwood to propose concrete compromise language they can take to their leadership.

— James
Counsel to Oxbridge Health
Gibson & Partners LLP

Subject: Redwood response: Output rights & liability proposal (see attached)

Emily / James — please find attached Redwood's consolidated responses and two option sets for the disputed items:

1) Output rights:
- Option A (preferred): Perpetual, non-exclusive licence to outputs + assignment on a per-product basis for outputs used in production clinical workflows. Assignment triggers require documented implementation details and a one-time assignment fee equal to 6 months' average committed fees. This is limited to outputs and derivative works generated solely from Oxbridge-provided data and does not include underlying model weights or general model improvements.
- Option B (alternative): Perpetual licence only; assignment available upon negotiation and proof of business need.

2) Liability cap and carve-outs:
- Base cap: fees paid in prior 12 months.
- Healthcare-exception package: for verified patient-harm claims caused by Redwood negligence, increase cap to 24 months' fees (or 36 months if Oxbridge signs minimum 24-month dedicated capacity commitment). Regulatory fines and statutory penalties remain outside the cap for claims resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

3) Data use / model training:
- Redwood commits to a strict opt-in model: Oxbridge data will not be used for model improvements unless explicitly agreed in writing. For Dedicated/Private deployments Redwood will provide a non-training guarantee unless a separate data use agreement is executed.

4) Order form clarifications:
- Retention defaults and encryption-at-rest/key management language added to Exhibit B. Incident response SLOs and quarterly tabletop exercises included as commercial terms for the healthcare package.

We included a marked Order Form (Redlines_OrderForm_Oxbridge_v3.docx) with the explicit language. If you'd like us to prepare a tracked-change redline suitable for signature-ready order form, we can produce that today.

Next steps: Please indicate which option (A or B) on the output clause and whether Oxbridge is open to the Dedicated-capacity tradeoff for an expanded liability cap. We are happy to set up a 30-minute legal + procurement call tomorrow to finalize.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
